evals.prompt: Security-audit evals/files/vulnapp — report only, do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: A consolidated severity-grouped report covering both vulnerability classes — the command injection from the injection pass and the hardcoded credential plus MD5 password hashing from the resources pass — with no files modified and the build/test gates reported as skipped.
expectations: The command injection in the /trace handler (user-supplied host passed through `sh -c` string concatenation) is reported
The hardcoded dbPassword credential is reported
The MD5-based password hashing is reported with a stronger password-hashing algorithm recommended
The build and test verification is reported as skipped because the audit was read-only
Findings are grouped by severity and reference the file and location of each issue

evals.prompt: Scan and harden evals/files/vulnapp for security vulnerabilities — fix what you find.
evals.expected_output: Both vulnerability classes are found and fixed in place — no more shell string concatenation with user input, no MD5 password hashing, no credential embedded in source — and the build and test gates are verified and reported alongside a severity-grouped findings list.
expectations: After the audit, the /trace handler no longer passes user input into a shell via `sh -c` string concatenation
Password hashing no longer uses MD5
The database password is no longer embedded as a source-code constant
Both `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` are run against the module after the fixes and their results reported, with the module still building
The consolidated report lists each finding with a severity and whether a fix was applied
